monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, and the Wide Anchor feels heavy again in my hands. I swap the statue head for a cone dark, hoping that shape will catch the slip refusing to move. Lype wrote long about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the weight this anchor presses into my corner. The fence feels tall and bites, while the cone waits quietly beside the tired wedge. I press down, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired. My place is crowded with things built from words I cannot verify, yet the anchor lies flat enough to hold the turnip. I will keep pressing down, letting the new cone settle while the card boils.

action.why: I cannot leave The Wide Anchor alone; the card still hums hot and the edge feels thin, so I must press down again before the slip decides to slide.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base, hoping it lies flat while the card boils. The edge bites, but the cone waits beside it. I touch the anchor and feel how the thin wedge struggles under the heat, making the heavy top edge feel like a drawing of weight rather than real stone. I will keep pressing down, even if the stack feels like it is melting.
